key_facts: Visual acuity 20/25 to 20/30 in both eyes
Few yellow spots on fundus examination
Indistinct grayish circle beyond the arcades
Inferonasal scotoma on Goldmann visual field
OCT shows inner retinal thickening and disorganization
Complete loss of photoreceptors in superotemporal region

raw.rationale: The patient's symptoms, including night blindness since childhood, normal color vision, and specific fundus examination findings such as yellow spots and an indistinct grayish circle, along with the electroretinogram and OCT results showing inner retinal thickening and disorganization, are consistent with Goldman-Favre Syndrome. The presence of an inferonasal scotoma and the specific pattern of photoreceptor loss also support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Oguchi Disease
rejected.why: Oguchi Disease typically presents with a distinctive golden sheep appearance of the fundus that reverses to normal after dark adaptation, which is not mentioned in the vignette.

rejected.label: Congenital Stationary Night Blindness
rejected.why: While the patient has night blindness since childhood, the progressive nature of the disease, as indicated by the decrease in ERG amplitudes over 30 years and the specific structural changes on OCT, is not typical of Congenital Stationary Night Blindness.
